data.description:

Traders use the roll trade period to square positions, adjust slates and net out any exposure.

Prices to roll positions from December to January was seen bid and offered between a 50 cent and $2 premium to US crude futures .

US energy firms this week added rigs for a second time in five weeks, energy services firm Baker Hughes said in its closely followed report.

The total oil and gas rig count, an early indicator of future output, rose by six to 607 in the week to November 20, its highest since April 26, 2024.

data.title: SUNation Energy Q3 Revenue Rises Sequentially to $11.2 Million; Net Loss $11.8 Million
data.description:
SUNation Energy reported third-quarter 2026 revenue of $11.2 million, up from $8.2 million in the second quarter, with gross margin improving to 30.8%. The company recorded an $11.8 million net loss, including $9.8 million in non-cash goodwill and intangible-asset impairment charges. Results continued to reflect weaker residential demand following the expiration of the federal residential solar tax credit.

Financial Highlights

  • Revenue was $11.20 million, down 41% from $18.99 million in the third quarter of 2025.
  • Gross profit was $3.45 million, compared with $7.21 million a year earlier; gross margin was 30.8%, versus 38.0%.
  • Operating loss was $11.71 million, compared with an operating loss of $246,000 in the prior-year quarter. Operating expenses included $9.82 million in goodwill and intangible-asset impairment charges.
  • Net loss was $11.82 million, or $1.81 per basic and diluted share, compared with a net loss of $393,000, or $0.12 per share, in Q3 2025.
  • Adjusted EBITDA was a loss of $822,341, compared with adjusted EBITDA of $897,850 in the prior-year quarter.

Business Highlights

  • Commercial and service work made up a larger portion of the business, representing approximately 33% of consolidated revenue, compared with approximately 18% a year earlier. Residential activity remained affected by the market’s adjustment to the expired federal tax credit.
  • Commercial activity was led by New York. Hawaii operations saw increased battery attachment and service work, partially offsetting lower residential installation volumes.
  • Hawaii Energy Connection’s battery attachment rate increased 13% year over year, with the company pursuing storage opportunities supported by Hawaii’s Bring Your Own Device Plus program.
  • SUNation amended its merger agreement with Suniva to address financing, stockholder approvals and closing requirements. The company currently anticipates closing in the first quarter of 2027, subject to required approvals and other conditions.
  • The company continued to focus on commercial projects, battery storage, maintenance and repair, roofing and adjacent energy services while managing operations through a period of lower residential demand.

Original SEC Filing: SUNation Energy, Inc. [ SUNE ] - 8-K - Nov. 20, 2026

data.title: Tech leads global stocks rout, Treasury yields fall
data.description:
Key points:
  • Broad index of global stocks in biggest weekly drop since 2020
  • Anthropic shares fall as much as 14.5% to just above IPO pricing
  • US bonds rally, spot gold and silver at 14-month lows
  • US chipmakers, Taiwan stocks each fall 17% for the week

By Rodrigo Campos

Tumbling technology-related shares led a global stock sell off on Friday, with US traders searching for safe havens as the US 10-year yield dropped by the most in a month.

Traders sold stocks in most markets with Japan and Korea down more than 5% overnight. Taiwanese shares TWSE:TAIEX were down 17% for the week, their biggest weekly decline since 1990, while on Wall Street chip-maker shares fell 10.7% Friday and 17.1% for the week.

Anthropic , which debuted this week, fell as much as 14.5% on its first full day of trading, just above its $83 IPO pricing, and ended down 9.1% at $88.30.

Consumer staples was the sole S&P 500 sector to end in the black on Friday.

"Markets are entering a more defensive phase," said Daniela Hathorn, senior market analyst at Capital.com.

"Strong AI demand and successful individual listings are no longer sufficient to sustain broader risk appetite when investors are questioning valuations, borrowing costs and the outlook for corporate profitability."

The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 949.73 points, or 1.93%, to 48,147.33; the S&P 500 CBOE:SPX fell 265.44 points, or 3.70%, to 6,910.39, and the Nasdaq Composite fell 1,261.47 points, or 5.28%, to 22,617.73.

MSCI's gauge of stocks across the globe EURONEXT:IACWI fell 34.89 points, or 3.30%, to 1,021.91. Its weekly decline of 8.1% was the largest since early 2020.

The pan-European STOXX 600 index fell 2%, emerging market stocks CBOE:EFS fell 3.10% and MSCI's broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan (.MISX00000PUS) closed lower by 3.27%. Japan's Nikkei fell 5.06%.

The VIX index, linked to the cost of insurance against a drop in the S&P 500, closed at its highest since April 2025 .

As investors sought safe-haven assets, government bonds rallied.

The yield on benchmark US 10-year notes fell 10.43 basis points to 4.948%, the largest daily drop since October 22. The 30-year bond (US30YT=RR) yield fell 6.81 basis points to 5.3329%. The 2-year note (US2YT=RR) yield, which typically moves in step with interest rate expectations for the Federal Reserve, fell 13.21 basis points to 4.647% even as a rate hike is priced in for next month's policy meeting.

DOLLAR FLAT, OIL RISES LATE

The dollar index was little changed after touching a 19-month high on Thursday. The dollar's recent rally has been fueled by bets on tighter monetary policy due to hotter-than-expected US inflation data.

"I think the momentum has stalled for the dollar ... but I think it's a little bit early to pick a top for the dollar," said Marc Chandler, chief market strategist at Bannockburn Capital Markets.

The dollar index fell 0.05% to 103.90, with the euro down 0.05% at $1.0961. Against the Japanese yen , the dollar weakened 0.67% to 158.6.

In commodities, crude prices rose late on Friday on worries about possible attacks in the US-Israeli war with Iran, and as traders bought crude ahead of next week's Thanksgiving holiday.

US crude rose 1.49% to $83.67 a barrel and Brent rose to $92.61 per barrel, up 0.68% on the day.

Gold prices fell to a 14-month low after the largest weekly drop in 8 months.

Spot gold fell 2.81% to $3,520.09 an ounce and spot silver fell 4.22% to $40.95 an ounce. Copper declined 2.9% to $12,162.50 a ton.

data.title: Plantify Foods Announces Adoption of Semi-Annual Reporting
data.description:
(TheNewswire)

    Toronto, Ontario – TheNewswire – November 20, 2026 — Plantify Foods, Inc. (TSXV: PTFY) ("Plantify Foods" or the "Company") announces that it has adopted a semi-annual financial reporting ("SAR") framework, effective immediately. This change is being made pursuant to the Coordinated Blanket Order 51-933 Exemptions to Permit Semi-Annual Reporting for Certain Venture Issuers ("CBO 51-933").

    CBO 51-933 allows eligible venture issuers to voluntarily move from a quarterly to a semi-annual financial reporting framework.

    Transition Details – Plantify’s fiscal year ends on December 31. Under the SAR framework, the Company will be exempt from filing interim financial reports and related Management Discussion & Analysis (“MD&A”) for its first and third quarters for so long as it continues to meet eligibility criteria under CBO 51-933.

    By adopting the SAR, Plantify aims to reduce the administrative and financial burden associated with quarterly reporting, allowing management to focus resources on advancement of different projects.

    • Initial Interim Period: The Company will not file an interim report for the third quarter (Q3) ending September 30, 2026 and for the first quarter (Q1) ending March 31, 2027.


    • Ongoing Reporting: Plantify will continue to file audited annual consolidated financial statements (due within 120 days of December 31, 2026), and six-month interim financial reports (due within 60 days of June 30).


    • Continued Disclosure: The Company remains committed to timely disclosure and will continue to report all material changes and significant developments as required under National Instrument 51-102.


    • Eligibility: Plantify confirms it meets the pilot program's eligibility criteria, which includes being a venture issuer with annual revenues of less than $10 million and maintaining a clean 12-month continuous disclosure record.


    • Continued Participation: Should the Company cease to continue participating in the SAR Pilot Program, it will announce it in a future news release.


    About Plantify Foods, Inc.

    Plantify Foods, Inc. (TSXV: PTFY) has had no business operations since its former operating subsidiary ceased operations in 2024 and is evaluating new business opportunities.

data.title: Enphase Energy to layoff about 320 employees
data.description:
Solar inverter maker Enphase Energy said on Friday it would reduce its workforce by 12%, or about 320 employees.

The company expects $25 million to $28 million in restructuring and asset impairment charges, with about $24 million to be recorded in the fourth quarter of 2026. Nearly $13 million of the charges are expected to be paid in cash.

Enphase in January cut roughly 160 jobs and moved certain functions to lower-cost regions as part of a plan to streamline operations and improve profitability.

data.title: Anthropic’s Day Two Drop Fuels Broader Tech Rout; Dan Ives Points To ‘Perfect Storm’
data.description:
Key points:
  • The Yorkville analyst, however, maintained that the multi-trillion-dollar AI infrastructure buildout remains on track and that the broader technology thesis into 2027 is intact.
  • On Friday, ANT stock traded lower, joining declines in Nvidia, AMD, and other AI-linked names as the Nasdaq and broader indexes remained under pressure.
  • “If sentiment for AI companies worsens, this actually helps $ANT in the long term, as they have done their job and can sleep soundly on capital for the next few years, while others will struggle,” Rihard Jarc said.

Tech stocks continued to slide on Friday as Anthropic (ANT) shares fell on their second day of trading, pulling down the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite 5%, a result that analyst Dan Ives said is being driven by a “perfect storm” created by multiple factors.

Dan Ives Points To A 'Perfect Storm'

Analyst Dan Ives attributed the selloff to a cluster of pressures: the Democratic “blue wave” midterm gains and resulting worries over anti-AI and data-center policies in key states and the abrupt exit of Nvidia’s Jensen Huang amid personal controversies, which the board has said will not lead to his return.

China-related regulatory scrutiny, Anthropic’s successful IPO, which drew capital away from other tech names, and hawkish Fed commentary aided the selloff, he said in an X post.

The Yorkville analyst, however, maintained that the multi-trillion-dollar AI infrastructure buildout remains on track and that the broader technology thesis into 2027 is intact.

Anthropic’s Volatile Debut

Anthropic priced its IPO at $83 per share and closed its first session on Thursday up 17% at $97.17, raising tens of billions in the largest offering on record and briefly making it one of the world’s most valuable public companies.

On Friday, however, the stock closed 8.5% lower, joining declines in Nvidia (NVDA), Advanced Micro Devices Inc (AMD), and other AI-linked names as the Nasdaq and broader indexes remained under pressure. All of the Magnificent 7 stocks also closed lower.

Uncover Alpha founder and Chief Investment Officer at New Era Funds Rihard Jarc said on Friday that he bought shares of Anthropic, arguing that the company has strengthened its position by cracking distillation techniques that make it harder for open-source models to catch up.

“What people fail to understand about $ANT is that, in recent months, the stakes of $ANT achieving a monopoly-like position have risen significantly,” Jarc wrote in an X post. “Even with US-based competition, $ANT, with their IPO, now has $250B in cash on the balance sheet and makes +$81B ARR.”

In an environment where training frontier models is becoming extremely expensive, he contended that Anthropic’s resources and enterprise focus give it an edge over rivals such as OpenAI, which face tougher funding conditions. The only two companies capable of chasing Anthropic based on spend on compute may end up being Alphabet and Meta Platforms, he said, adding that Meta’s focus is on the consumer and they won’t be able to focus deeply on enterprise like Anthropic.

“If sentiment for AI companies worsens, this actually helps $ANT in the long term, as they have done their job and can sleep soundly on capital for the next few years, while others will struggle,” Jarc said.

How Did ANT, ONEQ Retail Traders React?

On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around ANT stock stayed within the 'extremely bullish' territory over the past 24 hours, while message volume stayed at 'extremely high' levels.

Sentiment around the Fidelity Nasdaq Composite Index ETF (ONEQ), which tracks the Nasdaq Composite Index, rose from 'neutral' to 'bullish' territory, accompanied by 'high' message volume.

Despite the drop on Friday, ANT stock is currently trading at about $89, above its IPO price.

data.title: Singaporean extradited to face US charges over global insider trading scheme
data.description:
By Nate Raymond

A Singaporean man has been extradited to the US to face charges that he helped lead a global insider trading network that made tens of millions of dollars trading on confidential information about the finances and merger plans of numerous companies.

Zhi Ge, 35, made his initial appearance in federal court in Boston on Friday after he was extradited from Singapore to face securities fraud and money laundering charges following his arrest in his home country in 2024, the US Department of Justice said.

He is one of nine individuals overall charged with participating in what prosecutors allege was a years-long insider trading scheme that relied on tips from investment bankers and other corporate insiders.

Prosecutors say Ge led the scheme along with Samy Khouadja, a former investment banker in France, and Eamma Safi, who co-owned a French restaurant with Khouadja. The US considers most of the defendants, including Khouadja, fugitives.

A lawyer for Khouadja did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Safi, who has been in US custody since 2025, has pleaded not guilty.

A court in Singapore recently ordered Ge extradited to the US. He is scheduled to appear in federal court again on December 16 for an arraignment. His attorney did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Prosecutors allege Khouadja, Safi and Ge from 2016 to 2024 recruited bankers and others to supply them with inside information about a variety of publicly traded companies and paid insiders for their illicit tips.

Charging papers say Ge attempted to recruit additional insiders into the scheme and cite messages he sent in 2019 encouraging an actor friend in New York to introduce him to "investment bankers in big banks working in M&A specifically."

The indictment said tips allowed them to engage in insider trading ahead of announcements about various deals including AstraZeneca's 2020 planned $39 billion acquisition of Alexion Pharmaceuticals and Novartis's 2024 acquisition of MorphoSys for $2.9 billion.

Ge and others would also use "burner" cell phones and encrypted messaging apps to conceal their activity and would speak in code, referring to money as "greens" and a company's prospective merger partners as "girls" and "models."

Prosecutors said the defendants also leaked information they obtained to journalists to make a trading profit once the news became public.

data.title: Moody's lifts Portugal sovereign rating over debt reduction, growth outlook
data.description:
Global ratings agency Moody's raised Portugal's sovereign rating to "A2" from "A3" on Friday, saying the country was likely to maintain fiscal discipline and solid economic growth despite a fragmented domestic political environment.

The upgrade adds to signs of investor confidence in Portugal's fiscal turnaround after years of efforts to cut one of the euro zone's heaviest debt burdens.

The move also follows positive actions by peers, with Fitch upgrading Portugal and S&P revising its outlook to positive this year, citing the country's resilient economy and improving public finances.

"Portugal's robust growth prospects continue to be supported by recent reforms under its National Recovery and Resilience Plan as well as reforms to migration policy," Moody's said in a statement.

Portugal's centre-right minority government in October forecast an economic growth of 2.1% in 2027 and a small fiscal surplus despite a number of tax cuts.

The country's public debt burden has fallen sharply since peaking above 130% in 2020 and is projected to decline further to 84.5% of GDP in 2027 from 87.5% this year, reflecting years of fiscal consolidation.

Moody's held the sovereign's outlook at "stable," saying risks and potential upsides to Portugal's credit profile are balanced.

data.title: Moody's Boosts Portugal's Credit Ratings, Cites Debt Reduction Policies
data.description:
By Natalie Weger

Moody's boosted Portugal's sovereign debt rating on confidence that the country will continue to maintain effective debt reduction policies and economic growth amid a fragmented political environment.

The ratings agency on Friday upgraded the nation's long-term foreign- and local-currency issuer and local-currency senior unsecured ratings to A2 from A3.

The outlook remains stable amid faster-than-expected government debt reduction and more dynamic growth performance, Moody's said.

Portugal's National Recovery and Resilience plan and immigration policy reforms have supported sustainable economic growth, the ratings agency said.

Moody's expects Portugal's debt burden to decline from 89% of gross domestic product in 2025 to 84% by the end of 2027, and then below 80% by 2029.

Moody's also upgraded the senior unsecured local currency medium-term note program rating to A2, the foreign currency commercial paper rating to P-1 and local currency other short-term rating to P-1.

data.title: Moody's Upgrades Hungary Outlook, Citing Improved EU Relations
data.description:
By Katherine Hamilton

Moody's Ratings changed its outlook on Hungary's government to stable from negative.

Alongside that, it affirmed Hungary's Baa2 long-term issuer and senior unsecured ratings and its Baa2 foreign-currency senior unsecured shelf rating.

Moody's said the upgraded outlook reflects reforms and improvement in Hungary's relations with the European Union. That improved relationship has reduced governance-related risks.

Anti-corruption institutions in the country have also strengthened. Renewed access to E.U. resources, improved investor sentiment and a concrete fiscal consolidation program all support prospects of economic growth and lower debt.

The Baa2 ratings reflect a balance between Hungary's relatively high income levels and diversified economy with its elevated government debt and continuing policy constraints.

Moody's also upgraded the issuer rating of Hungary's national bank to stable from negative, affirming the Baa2 issuer rating. The bank's credit profile is closely intertwined with the government and is influenced by the same credit fundamentals, Moody's said.

Hungary's local and foreign currency ceilings remain unchanged at A1.
